html:
Joaquin Balaguer was a writer and lawyer who served Rafael Trujillo and then was president of the Dominican Republic three times, for 22 years in all, between 1960 and 1996.

Elected after the 1965 civil war with US support, he ruled from 1966 to 1978. His years brought road building, housing and growth, but also the killing of hundreds of opponents. He returned in 1986 and, though nearly blind, held power until 1996.

He built the vast Columbus Lighthouse for the 500th anniversary of Columbus's arrival in 1992, and the disputed elections of 1994 forced him to cut his last term short. He remained a power broker until his death at 95.
sum: Joaquin Balaguer was a writer and lawyer who served Rafael Trujillo and then was president of the Dominican Republic three times, for 22 years in all, between 1960 and 1996.
